items.title: Mississauga wants to hit pause on new data centre applications for a year amid community outcry
items.summary: Check out the top trending stories across Ontario this week,… Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9… Amid growing public concerns, council voted in favour of developing an interim bylaw for a one-year moratorium on data centres in Mississauga as staff review land-use and environmental policies Council voted in favour of a motion to have staff prepare an Interim Control Bylaw which would mean a one-year moratorium on new data centre applications. The bylaw will be considered by council for approval on Sept. 16. Mississauga is moving to halt new applications for data centres for up to a year as it works to develop new rules for an expanding industry that councillors say has outgrown the city’s existing framework. City council voted unanimously in favour of a motion at its July 29 meeting, brought forward by councillors Martin Reid and Sue McFadden. The motion directs staff to prepare an Interim Control Bylaw (ICBL) under the Planning Act to temporarily prohibit new applications for major data centres, including artificial intelligence, hyperscale and cloud computing facilities for a year. The move makes Mississauga the first Greater Toronto Area (GTA) city to do so. The ICBL will be considered by council for approval on Sept. 16.

items.title: Police arrest UK man at airport months after armed Mississauga carjacking
items.summary: A 24-year-old man from the United Kingdom has been arrested after Peel Regional Police allege he fled Canada following an armed carjacking in Mississauga earlier this year. According to investigators, the suspect returned to Toronto on an international flight on July 16 and was arrested upon landing at Pearson Airport on an outstanding Canada-wide warrant. The charges stem from a carjacking that occurred on Feb. m. in the area of Torbram Road and Derry Road East. Police say the victim was sitting inside a commercial vehicle when two masked suspects approached armed with handguns. The suspects allegedly pointed the firearms at the victim before forcing him from the vehicle and stealing it. Following an investigation by Peel Regional Police’s Central Robbery Bureau, officers identified Raheem Hartley, 24, of the United Kingdom, as one of the alleged suspects. Investigators say Hartley left Canada shortly after the carjacking. A Canada-wide warrant for his arrest was issued in December 2025 after police determined he had fled the country. When Hartley returned to Canada on July 16, officers arrested him at Toronto Pearson International Airport. Hartley has been charged with robbery, disguise with intent, and use of an imitation firearm while committing an offence.

items.title: Two centuries of history: Leslie Log House celebrates 200 years
items.summary: Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House remains a treasured link to Mississauga's early settlement history. Entertainment and activities | July 31, 2026 Members of the media and public are invited to attend a special celebration marking the 200th anniversary of the Leslie Log House, one of the oldest remaining log homes in Ontario. The event will recognize the site’s historical significance and its role in preserving Mississauga’s early settler history. m. m. Community programming continues including a tea room, art in the park and more! Members of Council, representatives from the City of Mississauga and the Streetsville Historical Society, along with community members and heritage enthusiasts. Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House is one of the oldest surviving log homes in Ontario and a designated heritage property. Operated in partnership with the Streetsville Historical Society, the house offers visitors a glimpse into life in early Upper Canada and serves as an important reminder of Mississauga’s rural and agricultural roots. More information on the Leslie Log House can be found on the City’s webpage. ca 905-615-3200, ext.
